original_test_intent: Inject a correctable Receiver Error into the approved PCH PCIe port and prove the selected port's ERRCORSTS.RE bit asserts while host, PCH endpoint and link remain healthy and the fault indicator stays off.
original_method: The FAE maps the physical PCH-attached endpoint to the Cscript port and pcieX/portY register hierarchy, verifies device and management dependencies, performs one approved CE/Receiver-Error injection, correlates the exact bit with Windows PCIe reporting and health, then restores BIOS state without retry.
manual_activity: The FAE approves the PCH port/X/Y mapping, checks endpoint usage, changes BIOS controls, injects one CE and restores settings. The agent may collect the exact ERRCORSTS.RE and health evidence.
required_inputs: Physical PCH endpoint/BDF to Cscript port and pcieX/portY map
Endpoint identity, activity and management-path dependency
ITP/CScripts build/hash and proof `ce` injects Receiver Error on this interface
Mandatory ERRCORSTS.RE plus Windows PCIe CE, link/device-health and optional BMC/UEFI oracle
Abort, OOB recovery and BIOS restoration plan
safety_requirements: Dedicated/quiesced endpoint and independent console when path risk exists
Fresh PCH port map; never infer X/Y
One approved Receiver-Error injection with before/after register/link state
Abort on wrong bit/target, fatal escalation, link/device loss or service impact
No automatic retry; restore and verify endpoint/PCH health
agent_execution_scope: Validate PCH mapping and collect read-only Cscript/register/Windows/link/BMC/UEFI evidence
Do not choose a port, change BIOS, inject, reset/retry or decide PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Approve PCH target and CE-to-RE semantics

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Snapshot PCH topology, selected ERRCORSTS, link and driver state; run one mapped CE; time-correlate RE bit assertion with Windows WHEA/AER; prove unchanged link/device health; restore/diff BIOS and status under the approved procedure.

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The required PCH port/X/Y values are unresolved; the source does not prove generic `errType='ce'` maps to Receiver Error; Windows conflicts with dmesg; and optional management logs leave the port-specific register plus Windows event as an unstated mandatory core.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The PCH Receiver-Error purpose is clear and can be resolved with a current map, package semantics and endpoint-safe recovery inputs.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 36 Wistron-System RAS-00756-V003: approve the physical PCH endpoint/BDF to Cscript port and pcieX/portY map, endpoint/management dependencies, ITP/CScripts version/hash and proof `errType='ce'` selects Receiver Error; define mandatory ERRCORSTS.RE/Windows PCIe CE and link/device-health oracle, recovery and BIOS restoration.

review_improvement: Makes the named Receiver Error bit and selected PCH endpoint the acceptance core instead of accepting generic PCH log text.
independent_technical_reasoning: The source provides a strong register-level signature—ERRCORSTS.RE—but leaves the physical endpoint, PCH port and X/Y hierarchy runtime-dependent. It also assumes the package's generic CE token produces that specific bit. Those identities must be proven together because a PCH root port may host an essential device. With a verified map and package contract, one bounded injection is feasible under operator control, so RPUC is appropriate and the unresolved mapping is recorded as a source conflict.
